asset.credit: Map: Eastern Telegraph Company, 1901, public domain

provenance.heading: Developer experience, mood-cable
provenance.image: the Eastern Telegraph Company's chart of its submarine cables, 1901.
provenance.source: File:1901 Eastern Telegraph cables.png
provenance.crop: 500, 470, 1060, 785. The routes are isolated by color (a pixel is a route where R minus max(G, B) exceeds 35), fitted to 800 by 450 separately and composited as ink after the tone step; ground blur 0.4, black 100, white 215; positive is the light file (black lines on paper). Isolating the routes alone and thickening them, at three crops, turned them into thick blobs on a noisy gray field; the hybrid keeps the grayscale ground and composites the routes as ink without thickening.

source.origin: File:Ahmed Karahisari - Karalama (calligraphy exercise) - Google Art Project.jpg

asset.credit: Calligraphy: Ahmed Karahisari, 16th century, public domain

provenance.heading: Design system, mood-calligraphy
provenance.image: Karalama, a calligraphy exercise sheet, ink on paper.
provenance.source: File:Ahmed Karahisari - Karalama (calligraphy exercise) - Google Art Project.jpg
provenance.crop: 310, 475, 1030, 880. A 16 by 9 window 720 pixels wide in the middle band of the sheet, holding a few strokes at 150 to 300 pixels of thickness instead of the whole field; the window stops above the crease that runs across the sheet at source rows 883 to 887, so no seam crosses the image. Black 40, white 215, no blur. The strokes render solid, the paper renders clean with the pounced ground marks as dots, and the edge consistency of each stroke is what the eye reads. The first crop (0, 500, 1341, 1254) showed the full-width field and read as overlapping chaos in the grid view.

asset.alt: A 32-point mariner's compass rose engraved by Emanuel Bowen, 1748, rendered as a two-tone dither

source.origin: File:1748 Bowen Mariner's Compass and Armillary Sphere - Geographicus - CircleofWinds-bowen-1747.jpg (local copy `scratchpad/photo/compass.jpg`, 1800 by 1140).

asset.credit: Engraving: Emanuel Bowen, 1748, public domain

provenance.heading: Status and plan, mood-compass
provenance.image: A Circle of Winds consisting of 32 points, commonly called the Mariners Compass, the left plate of a hand-colored engraving of a compass rose and an armillary sphere.
provenance.source: File:1748 Bowen Mariner's Compass and Armillary Sphere - Geographicus - CircleofWinds-bowen-1747.jpg (local copy `scratchpad/photo/compass.jpg`, 1800 by 1140).
provenance.crop: 40, 90, 1040, 652. The compass rose plate: the 32-point rose with its degree ring fills the left two thirds of the sheet, the engraved wall and the sky, clouds and ship to its right form a textured strip, and the blank gutter between the two plates is the right quarter of the sheet, where the credit plate sits on clean ground. The box starts inside the plate's border and stops above the ribbon's text; the two ribbon knots at the plate's foot show at the bottom corners of the rose. Black 60, white 225, and a 3 pixel minimum filter, the setting from the round five reserve test; the filter thickens the engraved hatching so the points read as solid and half-tone wedges instead of noise, and the compass-point labels become texture inside the wedges. Positive is the light file (black lines on paper).

asset.alt: NASA's Blue Marble, the Earth with the Western Hemisphere in daylight, rendered as a two-tone dither

source.origin: File:Blue Marble Western Hemisphere.jpg (local copy `scratchpad/photo/earth-night.jpg`, 1800 by 1800).
source.artist: NASA Earth Observatory, images by Reto Stöckli, based on data from NASA and NOAA; the Commons file is dated October 2, 2007

asset.credit: Image: NASA, Reto Stöckli, 2007, public domain

provenance.heading: Brand, mood-earth
provenance.image: The Blue Marble, Western Hemisphere, from NASA's Blue Marble Next Generation series: a composite of MODIS land and ocean data (2001 to 2004), a single day of clouds, sea ice, radar topography and city lights along the terminator, published in 2007.
provenance.source: File:Blue Marble Western Hemisphere.jpg (local copy `scratchpad/photo/earth-night.jpg`, 1800 by 1800).
provenance.crop: 49, -7, 3279, 1809. The disk spans 72 to 1722 across and 72 to 1730 down in the source (center 897, 901). The box is 3230 by 1816 and reaches past the right, top and bottom edges, where Pillow pads black, which is the source's own ground. Fitted to 800 by 450 this puts the disk at 820 pixels of diameter on the sheet, centered at x 420 and y 450, so it spans x 10 to 830 and y 40 to 860. Round nine's mood plate spans about x 851 to 1463, y 539 to 771; a cell count on the dark file finds 0 lit cells inside that rectangle (scratchpad `marble3/refit.py`, candidate b820x420), so the plate meets nothing. Round eight's box (-642, 35, 2437, 1767) centered an 860 pixel disk at x 800 for the credit-only plate, and that fit is superseded. The credit plate at the 15px credit spans x 1090 to 1462, y 729 to 771. Its top-left corner is 402 pixels from the disk center, 28 pixels inside the 430 radius, but that part of the disk is the night side over the South Pacific, which is ground in both files, so no rendered cell sits under the plate (0 of the 16,039 cells in the plate rectangle are paper in the dark file; the rightmost lit cell on the plate's top row is at x 1049). Round six's box (-1201, 35, 1878, 1767) centered the disk at x 1090 to leave room for a title plate at lower left; on the mood slide that plate no longer exists and the lower-right credit plate cut the rim over the South Pacific, so round eight recentered the disk. The plate stays at lower right, as on every mood slide.
provenance.tone: the red channel instead of luminance. In luminance the ocean and the cloud tones sit close together and the disk dithers to noise, which is why round five rejected the image. In the red channel the ocean drops toward black while land and cloud rise, so the oceans clip to ink and the continents and cloud bands render as texture; the city lights on the night side render as scattered single cells. Blur 0.6, black 80, white 210, gamma 1.0. Positive is the dark file: the disk on the ink ground. The light file is the inverse.
provenance.placement: after Why the redesign, the first dense slide of Brand, so the section runs opener, four content slides, the Blue Marble, three content slides, the Rosetta Stone, five content slides, opener. Round seven placed it after The mark, directly before the Design system opener, which made it a second opener. Kevin asked for the image ("also i like the blue marble"); round six had it as the Status and plan opener.
provenance.artist: NASA Earth Observatory, images by Reto Stöckli, based on data from NASA and NOAA; the Commons file is dated October 2, 2007.

asset.alt: Louisbourg lighthouse on its headland in a fall storm, rendered as a two-tone dither

source.origin: File:Louisbourg Lighthouse, waves breaking in a fall storm 1.jpg

asset.credit: Photograph: Ken Heaton, CC BY-SA 4.0

provenance.heading: Website, mood-lighthouse
provenance.image: Louisbourg Lighthouse, Nova Scotia, with waves breaking in a fall storm.
provenance.source: File:Louisbourg Lighthouse, waves breaking in a fall storm 1.jpg
provenance.crop: 300, 330, 1800, 1174. Drops most of the empty sky and the dark foreground; the tower on the right comes up to about 180 pixels wide and the breaking wave sits at sheet rows 380 to 500. Blur 0.5, black 0, white 212, gamma 0.8, plus an unsharp mask (radius 8, 180 percent, threshold 3) on rows 150 to 260 of the 800 by 450 frame, the sea band, so the spray separates from the lit water. The sky goes to paper, the sea band keeps its texture, and the heath dithers instead of clipping, so the dark twin shows a modulated field rather than a slab. The first crop (0, 150, 1800, 1162, blur 0.8, black 40) clipped the heath to solid ink.

asset.alt: The Rosetta Stone, its three scripts carved in rows, rendered as a two-tone dither

source.license: CC BY-SA 4.0. The dithered files are adaptations, so the credit line on the plate is required

asset.credit: Photograph: Hans Hillewaert, CC BY-SA 4.0

provenance.heading: Brand, mood-rosetta
provenance.image: The Rosetta Stone, the Ptolemaic decree of 196 BC carved in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek, British Museum.
provenance.source: File:Rosetta Stone.JPG (local copy `scratchpad/photo/rosetta.jpg`, 1539 by 1800).
provenance.crop: 0, 300, 1539, 1166. The upper body of the stone with its broken top edge against the dark ground, cover-fit to 800 by 450, so the stone fills the sheet and its right edge ends near x 1320. Blur 0.6, black 140, white 230, gamma 0.9. The high black point drops the stone's surface to ink and leaves the cut glyph rows as light lines, so the inscription reads as rows of text rather than a grey field; the earlier black points of 60 to 90 left a 50 percent screen with no edge. Positive is the dark file (light glyphs on an ink stone); the light twin reads as dark text on paper.
provenance.sentence: One decree carved in three scripts so every reader could read it. General Translation does the same for software: one source text, every language.
provenance.placement: after Values, where the Tower of Babel sat from round seven to round ten. Kevin: "change the tower of babel to something else. maybe rosetta stone".
provenance.license: CC BY-SA 4.0. The dithered files are adaptations, so the credit line on the plate is required.

asset.alt: A liquid metal diamond with two contour bands, rendered in Glyphfield, dithered

source.renderer: Chrome for Testing, ANGLE Metal (Playwright), recorded in OPENERS.md

asset.credit: Material: liquid metal, Paper Shaders, rendered in Glyphfield

provenance.heading: Prototemplate and Glyphfield
provenance.image: the liquid metal material in its diamond form, white chrome on a black ground: a rotated square about 620 pixels wide in the upper right of the sheet, with two contour bands and a rounded-rectangle highlight outlined in dark, on solid ink. It is made in Glyphfield, the section's own tool, and it is the only opener in liquid metal. Round ten put it in place of the Prism Light crop (see Rejected candidates).
provenance.source: Glyphfield (`/Users/kevinliu/repos/glyphfield`), route `/shader-preview?materialId=paper-liquid-metal&diagnostics=1&live=1` on the local dev server (port 3012), Paper Shaders' Liquid Metal family, rendered the way the two color openers were: Chromium (Playwright, `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=metal --ignore-gpu-blocklist`), 1600 by 900 viewport at device scale factor 2, `devicePixelsSupported` cleared on the `paperShaderMount` handle, `setMinPixelRatio(2)` and `setMaxPixelCount(3200 * 1800 + 1)`, buffer verified at 3200 by 1800. Uniforms passed through `setUniforms` (scratchpad `openers-60-79/glyphfield/hi/render.mjs`, variant `lm-gem-c5`): `u_colorBack #000000`, `u_colorTint #ffffff`, `u_softness 0.05`, `u_shiftRed 0`, `u_shiftBlue 0`, `u_contour 0.6`, `u_repetition 3`, `u_distortion 0.07`, `u_offsetX 0`, `u_offsetY 0`, `u_scale 0.5`, `u_shape 3` (the diamond; `u_shape 1` is the circle of the sphere runner-up). The frame is the second of the script's three samples, taken at about 4, 5.5 and 7 seconds of playback, saved as `hi/lm-gem-c5-s2.png` (3200 by 1800).
provenance.crop: -1325, 105, 2709, 2374 (4034 by 2269), computed from the object's bounding box in the source (pixels above 30, 1563 pixels across) so that the diamond is 620 pixels wide and centered at sheet x 1160, y 315. The box reaches past the source on the left and at the bottom, where Pillow pads black, the render's own ground. The diamond's lower-left facet ends right of and above the plate's top-right corner. On the sheet the plate spans 137, 463, 877, 771 (the title wraps to two lines, so it is taller than the one-line plates); the nearest lit cell is 83 pixels from that rectangle, measured on the render, and 110 pixels from the 500-top box the candidates were screened against, and no cell inside the plate or in the 30 pixel band around it is paper.
provenance.processing: black point 20, gamma 1.0. 8.3 percent of cells are paper. The upper facet edges, the two contour bands and the highlight's outline survive the screen as solid lines; the lower facets darken toward the ground, so the lower silhouette is carried by the bands. The dither sits only inside the object as shading, the way it sits inside the Lens Gate sphere on the Documentation opener. The light twin is a shaded diamond with black bands on paper.
provenance.sentence: This section covers prototemplate.com, the design lab and knowledge base, and glyphfield.com, the tooling behind it.

provenance.crop: 49, -7, 3279, 1809. The disk spans 72 to 1722 across and 72 to 1730 down in the source (center 897, 901). The box is 3230 by 1816 and reaches past the right, top and bottom edges, where Pillow pads black, which is the source's own ground. Fitted to 800 by 450 this puts the disk at 820 pixels of diameter on the sheet, centered at x 420 and y 450, so it spans x 10 to 830 and y 40 to 860. Round nine's mood plate spans about x 851 to 1463, y 539 to 771; a cell count on the dark file finds 0 lit cells inside that rectangle (scratchpad `marble3/refit.py`, candidate b820x420), so the plate meets nothing. Round eight's box (-642, 35, 2437, 1767) centered an 860 pixel disk at x 800 for the credit-only plate, and that fit is superseded. The credit plate at the 15px credit spans x 1090 to 1462, y 729 to 771. Its top-left corner is 402 pixels from the disk center, 28 pixels inside the 430 radius, but that part of the disk is the night side over the South Pacific, which is ground in both files, so no rendered cell sits under the plate (0 of the 16,039 cells in the plate rectangle are paper in the dark file; the rightmost lit cell on the plate's top row is at x 1049). Round six's box (-1201, 35, 1878, 1767) centered the disk at x 1090 to leave room for a title plate at lower left; on the mood slide that plate no longer exists and the lower-right credit plate cut the rim over the South Pacific, so round eight recentered the disk. The plate stays at lower right, as on every mood slide.
provenance.tone: the red channel instead of luminance. In luminance the ocean and the cloud tones sit close together and the disk dithers to noise, which is why round five rejected the image. In the red channel the ocean drops toward black while land and cloud rise, so the oceans clip to ink and the continents and cloud bands render as texture; the city lights on the night side render as scattered single cells. Blur 0.6, black 80, white 210, gamma 1.0. Positive is the dark file: the disk on the ink ground. The light file is the inverse.
provenance.placement: after Why the redesign, the first dense slide of Brand, so the section runs opener, four content slides, the Blue Marble, three content slides, the Rosetta Stone, five content slides, opener. The compass rose plate: the 32-point rose with its degree ring fills the left two thirds of the sheet, the engraved wall and the sky, clouds and ship to its right form a textured strip, and the blank gutter between the two plates is the right quarter of the sheet, where the credit plate sits on clean ground. The box starts inside the plate's border and stops above the ribbon's text; the two ribbon knots at the plate's foot show at the bottom corners of the rose. Black 60, white 225, and a 3 pixel minimum filter, the setting from the round five reserve test; the filter thickens the engraved hatching so the points read as solid and half-tone wedges instead of noise, and the compass-point labels become texture inside the wedges. provenance.crop: 500, 470, 1060, 785. The routes are isolated by color (a pixel is a route where R minus max(G, B) exceeds 35), fitted to 800 by 450 separately and composited as ink after the tone step; ground blur 0.4, black 100, white 215; positive is the light file (black lines on paper). Isolating the routes alone and thickening them, at three crops, turned them into thick blobs on a noisy gray field; the hybrid keeps the grayscale ground and composites the routes as ink without thickening.
